C1.rationale: Anchor level 1: 'Collaboration/teamwork appears in learning outcomes, but no core unit assesses it.' Collaborative learning and team work recur as generic-skills/graduate-attribute claims across the program, but no assessment description in any core subject names a group project, client/stakeholder work, or interprofessional activity — every assessed task (reports, written assignments, presentations, exams) is described as an individual deliverable. No human-plus-tool coordination is documented anywhere, so level 3 does not apply.
evidenceLines: Demonstrate a capacity to successfully engage in collaborative activities such as group-based work and activities; and
Collaborative learning and team work;
Collaborative learning; problem solving; team work

C2.rationale: ACCT90039 ('Critically evaluate accounting research employing experiments and other methods of behavioural research') and ACCT90044/ACCT90045 ('Critically assess research design choices...') carry assessed written work (written assignment 35%; research proposal 50%) that operationalises critique of published research design — plausibly level 2's 'structured critique.' The extract never documents the marking criteria or rubric structure behind that critique. Ambiguous between level 1 ('appears in outcomes... but no core unit assesses it against criteria') and level 2 ('criterion-referenced appraisal'); per the ambiguity rule, scored at the lower level and recorded in ambiguities. No reliance-decision or AI-judgement evidence exists for level 3.
evidenceLines: Critically evaluate accounting research employing experiments and other methods of behavioural research.
Critically assess research design choices in the context of specific research questions in the chosen area of accounting research.

C3.rationale: 'Using computer software' (ACCT90011), 'Application of Windows software' and 'Using and designing computer programs' (ECOM90013) are the only digital-tool content in the extract, appearing as generic-skills lines on core (non-elective) subjects — squarely level 1's 'tool operation/training.' No line addresses AI capabilities, limitations, ethics, governance, or use-with-limits, so level 2 and above are not reached.
evidenceLines: Using computer software
Application of Windows software
Using and designing computer programs

C4.rationale: Demoted from level 3 on review: one of the three cited evidence lines ('Independently research the project topic, using a wide range of source material; and') is drawn from ACCT90003's Intended Learning Outcomes section, not its Assessment page — outcome-statement evidence that cannot establish an assessed level-3 claim. The remaining two lines (the two 5000-word report assessment descriptions) confirm only that a substantial, individually-supervised report is graded; they say nothing about the student choosing the topic, which is what the self-scoped claim requires. The Overview-page language that would actually establish self-scoping (Director approval of topic; 'collect data to test their theoretical framework and prepare a manuscript...') was never quoted in evidenceLines. As cited, the evidence clears level 2 ('application to novel or unfamiliar problems') — a compulsory, individually-supervised, 100%-weighted (80%-hurdle on ACCT90043) empirical research report — but not level 3.
evidenceLines: Independently research the project topic, using a wide range of source material; and
A 5000 (+/- 10%) word report, with the word limit to be agreed upon in consultation with the supervisor

C5.rationale: ACCT90003/ACCT90043 require students to 'collect data to test their theoretical framework' — primary evidence generation, required (not elective) and assessed (100% weight report, 80% hurdle on ACCT90043). Level 3 additionally requires the methodology to be 'defended under scrutiny (viva, defence, or staged supervised review).' The extract shows supervisor assignment, Director approval of topic, and a manuscript that is 'workshopped' before submission, which could constitute staged supervised review, but no line uses viva/defence/examination language for the methodology itself. Ambiguous between level 2 and level 3; scored at the lower level and recorded in ambiguities.
evidenceLines: The subject will also require students to collect data to test their theoretical framework and prepare a manuscript that can be workshopped and submitted for publication in a leading accounting research journal.
The Director of the Doctoral Program in Accounting or their nominee must approve the topic and, in discussion with the student, assign a supervisor.
Hurdle requirement: 80%

W1.rationale: 'Clearly communicate, both orally and in written form, their research ideas' is a course-level outcome. Core assessment adds presentation to peers/staff — seminar presentations (ACCT90019, ACCT90020, ACCT90039) and a Formal Presentation 'in the final workshop' (ACCT90044/45) — but every documented audience is the subject's own workshop/seminar (supervisors, academic staff, cohort peers). No line documents a recognised professional genre (client brief, consultancy/policy advice, pitch) or an audience beyond the teaching team, so level 2 is not reached.
evidenceLines: Clearly communicate, both orally and in written form, their research ideas and their evaluation of the research ideas and procedures from the accounting research literature.
Seminar presentations and class participation
In the final workshop held in the second last week of Semester 2

W2.rationale: ACCT90003/ACCT90043 require students to identify a research question, collect data, and produce a manuscript intended 'for publication in a leading accounting research journal' — a real research task producing the artefact a professional researcher would produce, judged via supervisor and Director involvement: level 2. Level 3 requires this to be the assessment spine AND carry a genuine constraint of practice. The Year 2 core (ACCT90003, ACCT90043, ACCT90044, ACCT90045) forms a plausible scaffolded spine toward the manuscript, but the extract does not document a genuine practice constraint (external audience, real resource/time limits, or the profession's own stated performance standard) for the assessed deliverable. Ambiguous between level 2 and level 3; scored at the lower level and recorded in ambiguities.
evidenceLines: The subject will also require students to collect data to test their theoretical framework and prepare a manuscript that can be workshopped and submitted for publication in a leading accounting research journal.

W3.rationale: No line in the extract mentions a placement, practicum, internship, client project, or community-based project anywhere in the course structure. The subject-level 'supervisor' relationships in ACCT90003/ACCT90043/ACCT90044/ACCT90045 are academic research supervision, not placement in a workplace or professional-community setting with practitioner supervision. Matches level 0.
evidenceLines: Students in the Master of Commerce (Accounting) will need to complete 16 subjects, comprising ten compulsory accounting subjects, one economics subject, one econometric subject and four electives.

ambiguities: C2: ACCT90039, ACCT90044 and ACCT90045 assess 'critically evaluate'/'critically assess research design choices' as ILOs via written assignments and a research proposal, which could read as criterion-referenced structured critique (level 2), but the extract documents no explicit marking criteria/rubric structure, so scored at the lower level 1.

C4: On review, one of the three evidenceLines cited for level 3 came from an Intended Learning Outcomes section rather than an Assessment page, and no genuine assessment-page evidence establishes that the student chooses the research topic (the Director approves it). Demoted to level 2 — a compulsory, individually-supervised, 100%-weighted empirical research report. A fresh capture that quotes the Overview-page self-scoping language (Director approval process, primary-data collection, workshop/publication track) directly from an Assessment-linked source could support re-scoring to level 3.

C5: ACCT90003/ACCT90043 are required, primary-data research projects with supervisor assignment, Director approval of topic, and manuscripts 'workshopped' before submission — this could satisfy level 3's 'staged supervised review' of methodology, but the extract never uses viva/defence/examination language for the methodology itself, so scored at the lower level 2.

W2: The Year 2 core sequence (ACCT90003, ACCT90043, ACCT90044, ACCT90045) forms a scaffolded progression toward a publication-track research manuscript, which could satisfy level 3's assessment-spine criterion, but no line in the extract documents a genuine constraint of practice (external audience, real resource/time limits, or the profession's stated performance standard), so scored at the lower level 2.
